text:
maria: noticing a recurring p95 spike on dedicated-rt around 12:36 UTC, correlates with a burst of short (<=64) seq requests. latency graphs show 120ms -> 380ms for a subset of requests. can someone check kernel selection logs?
leo: saw that too, looks like the runtime is picking the generic float kernel instead of the optimized int8 path for a handful of shards. weird because model config didn't change.
ankur: could be falling back due to mismatched sequence length or kv-cache shape. we had a recent heuristic tweak that forces conservative kernel choices when batch shape variance > 0.3.
maria: here's the grep from one host (trimmed):
```
[12:36:11] kernel_select: model=redwood-v2-s, seq=16, batch=8 -> selected=generic_fp32, reason="variant_mismatch"
[12:36:11] kv_cache: entries=128MB, miss_rate=0.18, eviction=LRU
[12:36:11] batch_scheduler: microbatch=4, admitted=12, queued=3
```
leo: thanks. the "variant_mismatch" tag is new from the kernel-heuristics change two days ago (PR #412). ci-bot shows that rollout targeted canaries only but maybe a wider push happened.
ci-bot: deploy: cluster/dedicated-rt post-deploy checks passed (2026-03-15T12:30:01Z) — rollout: 25% -> 100% over 6m (triggered by ops).
ankur: if kv_cache miss_rate spikes you can get more cache warming traffic which ups variance in sequence lengths (clients retry with shorter prefixes). that can push the heuristics over threshold and force generic kernel use — expensive.
maria: profiler snippets (short):
```
perf: tokens/sec median=8.5k, p95 drop from 7.2k -> 2.1k during window
cpu kernel_generic: 48% -> 70%
cuda optimized_kernel: 30% -> 9%
```
leo: suggests we revert the conservative branch in kernel-heuristics or relax the variance threshold to 0.5 as a hotfix. also check admission control microbatch sizing: if microbatch target is too small we lose batching efficiency.
ankur: quick mitigation: 1) relax kernel variance threshold on canary hosts 2) increase microbatch cap from 8->16 for short-seq queues 3) raise kv-cache size slightly to reduce eviction churn. any objections?
maria: I'll patch a runtime config change for the canary pool and run a 10m test. can someone run a synthetic traffic replay that mirrors short-seq distribution?
leo: running replay on pool-3 now: command I'm using:
```
./tools/replay --model redwood-v2-s --dist short-seq --qps 400 --duration 600 --label "kernel-fallback-repro"
```
sre-bot: alert: host i-0a3f kernel_fallback rate increased by 3.2x at 12:36 UTC — auto-scaling triggered (scale +2 GPUs).
ankur: note scaling will mix newer and older kernel-enabled shards, might mask repro. prefer a fixed-size canary set.
maria: good point. I'll pin the canary to the original kernel commit and apply the relaxed threshold only there.
leo: post-replay numbers: p95 back to ~130ms on canary after threshold tweak, tokens/sec recovered to ~6.9k. baseline still noisy on non-canary.
ankur: we'll open a follow-up issue to tighten heuristics later and add a unit test that simulates seq-length variance. also add a metric for "kernel_fallback_count" per shard.
maria: created issue ENG-9873 and assigned to runtime-kernels. canary will be kept for 2h, ops to monitor. thanks all. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: note: rolled hotfix config to canary pool (config/kernel/variance_threshold=0.5) at 12:52 UTC.
